columns.name: acq_time
columns.description: The entry's instant in ISO-8601 with its UTC offset (e.g. ``2026-02-03T09:00:00+00:00``). The only timestamp a row carries, and BIDS' own name for it: ``pd.to_datetime(df.acq_time)`` reads it offset-aware in one step. Older files that split the instant across ``date``, ``time`` and a free-text ``timezone`` are read and folded into this column; only ``acq_time`` is ever written.

columns.name: block_id
columns.description: Index of the stimulation block within a session. Every row of one block repeats its stimulation values.

columns.name: append_id
columns.description: Data-entry episode within this file: increments each time the file is reopened to add rows. File-scoped, so equal values in different files are unrelated. Deliberately not called ``session_id``, which BIDS uses for the ``ses-`` label in ``sessions.tsv``; one name for both meanings would mislead every reader of a combined table.

columns.name: is_initial
columns.description: ``1`` for the baseline block recorded before any configuration is tried; ``0`` for a recording block.

columns.name: is_final
columns.description: ``1`` on the rows of the block the patient was left on at the end of the visit, as marked by the clinician; ``0`` elsewhere. Empty in older files; no block is ``1`` when the clinician did not mark one.

columns.name: is_starred
columns.description: ``1`` on the rows of a block the clinician starred during the visit as a particularly good configuration; ``0`` elsewhere. Any number of blocks may be starred. A star records a clinical impression, not a ranking. Empty in older files.

columns.name: scale_name
columns.description: Clinical or session scale name (or newline-separated names).

columns.name: scale_value
columns.description: Scale value, or ``n/a`` when the scale was not assessed at this block.

columns.name: pathology
columns.description: Condition being treated, chosen once for the session from the app's list (``PD``, ``ET``, ``Dystonia``, ``OCD``, ``MDD``, ``TS``) or typed. The same on every row. Empty in older files.

columns.name: target
columns.description: Anatomical target of the leads (e.g. ``STN``, ``GPi``, ``VIM``), chosen once for the session. The same on every row. Empty in older files.

columns.name: left_electrode_model
columns.description: Left lead model, as named in ``schema/electrode_models.json``. Older files have one ``electrode_model`` column for both leads, which is read as both.

columns.name: right_electrode_model
columns.description: Right lead model, as named in ``schema/electrode_models.json``. The same as the left when both leads are the same model.

columns.name: ipg_model
columns.description: Implanted pulse generator model, as named in ``schema/electrode_models.json`` or typed. Recorded only: the app does not change any setting from it. Empty in older files.

columns.name: program_id
columns.description: Stimulation program label (e.g., ``A``, ``B``).

columns.name: left_stim_freq
columns.description: Left stimulation frequency.

columns.name: left_anode
columns.description: Left anode contact(s) in the contact grammar: ``case`` for the can, ``E2`` for a ring, ``E2b`` for one segment, ``_`` joining several.

columns.name: left_cathode
columns.description: Left cathode contact(s), same grammar as ``left_anode``.

columns.name: left_amplitude
columns.description: Left amplitude in mA. A single value, or per-contact values joined by ``_`` in ``left_cathode`` order when current is steered (``3.3_2.2`` is 5.5 mA split 60/40). It carries no ``Units`` because a steered value is not a single number; sum the parts for the delivered current.

columns.name: left_pulse_width
columns.description: Left pulse width.

columns.name: right_stim_freq
columns.description: Right stimulation frequency.

columns.name: right_anode
columns.description: Right anode contact(s), same grammar as ``left_anode``.

columns.name: right_cathode
columns.description: Right cathode contact(s), same grammar as ``left_anode``.

columns.name: right_amplitude
columns.description: Right amplitude in mA, same shape as ``left_amplitude``.

columns.name: right_pulse_width
columns.description: Right pulse width.

columns.name: medications
columns.description: Medications as recorded in the initial assessment, free text. Written on the initial-assessment rows (``is_initial`` ``1``) and empty on the others.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text note recorded at this block.

columns.name: acq_time
columns.description: The entry's instant in ISO-8601 with its UTC offset (e.g. ``2026-02-03T09:00:00+00:00``). The only timestamp a row carries, and BIDS' own name for it: ``pd.to_datetime(df.acq_time)`` reads it offset-aware in one step. Older files that split the instant across ``date``, ``time`` and a free-text ``timezone`` are read and folded into this column; only ``acq_time`` is ever written.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text note for this entry.

columns.name: participant_id
columns.description: Subject label as ``sub-<label>``, parsed from the source filename. The BIDS spelling and value shape deliberately, so this table joins directly onto ``participants.tsv``.

columns.name: session_id
columns.description: Session label as ``ses-<label>``, parsed from the source filename: the BIDS session, as ``sessions.tsv`` means it. Not to be confused with ``append_id``, the data-entry counter within one source file, which older files spell ``session_id``.

columns.name: run_id
columns.description: The BIDS run index, zero-padded, without the ``run-`` prefix so it sorts numerically.

columns.name: source_file
columns.description: The session or notes file this row came from. A notes file gives one row per note, with only ``acq_time`` and ``notes`` filled. Not redundant with the entities above: ``run`` defaults to ``01`` and does not auto-increment, so two visits on the same day can share all three, and this is then the only thing that tells their rows apart. A block is unique across the table on ``(participant_id, session_id, run_id, block_id)``.
